title: County of Pallars
capsule: The County of Pallars was a march county in the Pyrenean valleys of the upper Noguera Pallaresa (modern Catalonia), which broke free of Toulousain control around 872 under Raymond I, its first independent count. Raymond pursued frontier warfare against al-Andalus, built defensive towers, and sought to establish a local diocese to underpin the county's autonomy; on his death the territory was inherited jointly by his sons, beginning a long pattern of shared rule among brothers and cousins. The tenth century brought obscurity and economic decline as Pallars fell under the competing influence of Urgell, Barcelona, and Aragon. The unified county effectively ended around 1011 with the death of Sunyer I, when his sons partitioned it into Pallars Jussà and Pallars Sobirà.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's Pyrenean mountain territory is broadly identifiable with modern watershed geography and corroborated by Carolingian and comital charters; precise early medieval frontiers with neighbouring counties are poorly documented.
